When Mommy/Daddy is Tired

A short read-aloud for little hearts when grown-ups need a quiet moment on the couch.

Read-aloud

Sometimes Mommy or Daddy looks tired. Their eyes might be heavy, their voice quiet, or they need to rest on the couch. It’s okay. Everyone gets tired sometimes—even grown-ups.

Jesus understands tired. He walked many miles with His friends, teaching and helping people all day. At times He got in a boat just to rest a little. One day He was so tired that He fell asleep in the boat while a storm came. But He still had peace.

And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? Mark 4:38 (KJV)

God gives us rest. When Mommy or Daddy is tired, you can help in small ways: be gentle with your voice, pick up your toys without being asked, or sit quietly with a book for a few minutes. Those little things are love.

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Matthew 11:28 (KJV)

One small gentle step together

When you see Mommy or Daddy is tired:

  1. Speak softly.
  2. Do one helpful thing without being told.
  3. Pray a short prayer for them (even just “Jesus, help Mommy rest”).

A simple prayer

Dear Jesus, thank You for Mommy and Daddy. When they feel tired, please give them Your rest and strength. Help me be gentle and helpful today. Amen.

Coloring idea

A tired mommy or daddy resting peacefully on a couch, a small child nearby quietly reading or coloring—soft warm light, calm family warmth. Open the Verse Image generator (template T17) and paste the prompt from the Kids home card if you want a line-art sheet.
